# status


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

These helpers return feedback and loading markup without running the
underlying operation. You control the application state and decide when
to add, update, or remove each component.

``` python
from fasthtml.common import Form
from answerui.demo import demo
from fastcore.test import *
```

## Notice

`_notice` builds the shared inner structure for `Alert` and `Toast`: a
`Stack` of content beside an optional quiet icon close button marked
`dismiss`. Shared CSS styles the flex row, surface, and expanding
content column.

## Alert

`Alert` renders a message and optional supporting content on a tinted
accent surface (`[alert]`). Pass `ui_tone` (`'warning'`, `'danger'`,
`'success'`, or `'info'`) to choose a severity hue. With
`dismissible=True`, clicking the close button removes the alert through
the delegated `click` listener in `browser.js`. Because that listener is
attached to `document`, alerts inserted later by htmx are dismissible
without extra wiring.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Alert

``` python
def Alert(
    *c, dismissible:bool=False, **attrs
):
```

*An in-page message with optional dismissal*

Severity colour and screen-reader announcements are separate choices.
`Alert` adds no `role` by default because a persistent warning need not
interrupt a screen-reader user. For polite feedback, place an empty
`role="status"` region in the page first, then insert or update the
message inside it. Reserve `role="alert"` for urgent messages. Screen
readers do not reliably announce a message when a single swap creates
the live region with the message already inside it. See [ARIA live
regions](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Guides/Live_regions).

``` python
Alert.demo()
```

``` html
<div stack>
  <div alert ui-tone="success">
    <div stack>Your changes have been saved.</div>
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="quiet" btn-icon aria-label="Close" dismiss><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewbox="0 0 24 24" height="24px" width="24px" class="lucide-icon "><use href="#lc-x"></use></svg></button>  </div>
  <div alert ui-tone="warning">
    <div stack>
      <h3>Storage is nearly full</h3>
      <p>Remove unused files or choose a larger plan.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div alert ui-tone="danger">
    <div stack>The upload failed. Your original file has not changed.</div>
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="quiet" btn-icon aria-label="Close" dismiss><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewbox="0 0 24 24" height="24px" width="24px" class="lucide-icon "><use href="#lc-x"></use></svg></button>  </div>
</div>
```

Alerts have no auto-dismiss timer because important information must
stay visible until the user reads or closes it.

## Toast

Place an empty `Toaster()` in the page before delivering messages to it.
`Toaster` renders a polite live region (`role="status"`,
`aria-live="polite"`) with `popover="manual"`. When a `[toaster]`
mounts, `browser.js` calls `showPopover()`. Because it is a manual
popover, the browser draws it above ordinary page content and leaves it
open when the user clicks outside or presses Escape. Pass
`toaster_position` (`'top-start'`, `'bottom-start'`, or `'bottom-end'`)
to move it from the default top-end corner. A modal dialog opened later
sits above the toaster. Put feedback needed during a modal interaction
inside that dialog.

By default, `Toast` sets `--toast-duration: 5000ms` (controlled by
`life`) for the `ui-toast-lifetime` CSS animation. While the pointer
hovers over a toast or keyboard focus is inside it, CSS pauses that
animation (`animation-play-state: paused`). When `animationend` fires
for `ui-toast-lifetime`, `browser.js` removes the toast. Passing
`life=None` omits `--toast-duration` to keep the toast visible until the
user dismisses it. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, `--motion`
drops to `0ms` while `--toast-duration` stays unchanged.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Toaster

``` python
def Toaster(
    *c, **attrs
):
```

*The page’s polite live region for toast deliveries*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Toast

``` python
def Toast(
    *c, life:int=5000, dismissible:bool=True, oob:bool=False, **attrs
):
```

*A brief message for the toast region*

Deliver a toast inside an out-of-band wrapper with
`Div(Toast('Saved'), hx_swap_oob='beforeend:[toaster]')` or
`Toast('Saved', oob=True)`. During a `beforeend` swap, htmx discards the
outer element and appends its children. Wrapping the toast keeps the
`[toast]` element, its attributes, and its dismiss button intact.
Putting `hx_swap_oob` directly on `Toast` would make htmx discard the
`[toast]` element and append only its inner nodes. See [out-of-band
swaps](https://htmx.org/attributes/hx-swap-oob/).

The example below stores the out-of-band wrapper in a `template` element
whose HTML the button’s `hx-on:click` handler passes to
[htmx.swap](https://htmx.org/api/#swap). This demonstrates delivery
without a server or a registered behavior. In an app, return the wrapper
directly from a route with no inline script. Click the button to deliver
both messages, then try hovering or focusing the timed toast.

``` python
Toast.demo(height='14rem')
```

``` html
<div>
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="secondary" hx-on-click="htmx.swap(this, document.getElementById('_QghFrhnpQxuqzKbR3qxaDQ').innerHTML, {swapStyle: 'none'})">Deliver notifications</button><template id="_QghFrhnpQxuqzKbR3qxaDQ">    <div hx-swap-oob="beforeend:[toaster]">
      <div toast ui-tone="success" style="--toast-duration: 5000ms; ">
        <div stack>Your changes have been saved.</div>
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="quiet" btn-icon aria-label="Close" dismiss><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewbox="0 0 24 24" height="24px" width="24px" class="lucide-icon "><use href="#lc-x"></use></svg></button>      </div>
      <div toast ui-tone="danger">
        <div stack>The upload failed. Your original file has not changed.</div>
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="quiet" btn-icon aria-label="Close" dismiss><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewbox="0 0 24 24" height="24px" width="24px" class="lucide-icon "><use href="#lc-x"></use></svg></button>      </div>
    </div>
</template>  <div popover="manual" role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="false" aria-relevant="additions text" toaster></div>
</div>
```

### Queued toasts

A redirect response contains no HTML for a toast. An htmx route returns
a partial fragment rather than a full page with a `Toaster`. In both
cases, call `add_toast(sess, msg, life=5000, **attrs)` to queue the
message in the session under `toasts_key` (`'aui_toasts'`), passing
severity as an attribute such as `ui_tone='success'`.

On a full-page route, render queued toasts inside
`Toaster(*pop_toasts(sess))`. On a fragment route, include
`toasts_oob(sess)` in the response for htmx to swap into the existing
`[toaster]`. Call `setup_toasts(app)` to register `toast_after` on
`app.after` and inject `toasts_oob(sess)` automatically on every markup
or empty response. `toast_after` does nothing when the queue is empty,
as happens after a full-page route calls `pop_toasts(sess)`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Queue two messages as a route does and pop them with `toasts_oob`,
clearing `sess`:

``` python
sess = {}
add_toast(sess, 'Your changes have been saved.', ui_tone='success')
add_toast(sess, 'The upload failed. Your original file has not changed.', life=None, ui_tone='danger')
oob = toasts_oob(sess)
test_eq(sess, {})
test_eq([t.attrs.get('ui-tone') for t in oob.children], ['success', 'danger'])
oob
```

<div hx-swap-oob="beforeend:[toaster]">
  <div toast ui-tone="success" style="--toast-duration: 5000ms; ">
    <div stack>Your changes have been saved.</div>
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="quiet" btn-icon aria-label="Close" dismiss><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewbox="0 0 24 24" height="24px" width="24px" class="lucide-icon "><use href="#lc-x"></use></svg></button>  </div>
  <div toast ui-tone="danger">

<button type="button" btn btn-variant="quiet" btn-icon aria-label="Close" dismiss><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewbox="0 0 24 24" height="24px" width="24px" class="lucide-icon "><use href="#lc-x"></use></svg></button>  </div>
</div>

## Progress

`Progress` wraps the native `<progress>` element (`progress[progress]`).
Pass `value` and `max` when the completed fraction is known, or omit
`value` for an indeterminate bar. The `[progress]` CSS rule sets only
`inline-size: 100%`, `block-size: var(--space-2)`, and
`accent-color: var(--color-accent)` without changing the browser’s
native rendering or animation. Wrap the bar in a `Label` describing the
operation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Progress

``` python
def Progress(
    *c, **attrs
):
```

*Native progress; omit value when the amount completed is unknown*

A labelled bar for a known amount of work, and an indeterminate one for
an unknown amount:

``` python
Progress.demo()
```

``` html
<div stack>
<label stack class="gap-1">Importing files<progress progress value="40" max="100"></progress></label><label stack class="gap-1">Waiting for the server<progress progress></progress></label></div>
```

## Spinner

`Spinner` renders a `Span` (`[spinner]`) with a CSS ring (`::before`)
beside visible status text (`label`, defaulting to `'Loading...'`). The
ring uses the `ui-spin` animation with duration
`calc(var(--motion) * 5)`. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the
animation stops while the label remains visible. As with `Alert`, add a
live-region `role` only when screen readers should announce the status.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Spinner

``` python
def Spinner(
    label:str='Loading...', **attrs
):
```

*A small spinning ring with visible text explaining the wait*

``` python
Spinner.demo()
```

``` html
<span spinner>Checking the connection…</span>
```

## Skeleton

`Skeleton` renders an unanimated block placeholder (`Span` with
`[skeleton]` and `aria-hidden="true"`) that reserves layout space before
content arrives. By default it spans `inline-size: 100%` and
`block-size: 1em` with `var(--n-1)` background and `var(--radius-1)`
corners. Override those dimensions with CSS such as `style`. Because
`aria-hidden="true"` hides the placeholder from the accessibility tree,
provide a separate visible loading message for screen readers.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Skeleton

``` python
def Skeleton(
    **attrs
):
```

*A decorative placeholder for content that has not loaded*

``` python
Skeleton.demo()
```

``` html
<div stack>
  <p>Loading the project summary…</p>
  <section card aria-busy="true" stack>
<span skeleton aria-hidden="true" style="inline-size: 40%; block-size: 1.5em"></span><span skeleton aria-hidden="true"></span><span skeleton aria-hidden="true" style="inline-size: 75%"></span>  </section>
</div>
```

The loading message is outside the busy region. When the content
arrives, replace the placeholders and clear `aria-busy`, or replace the
whole card. `Skeleton` does not make these changes itself.
